subject: Mental Models
title: Margin of Safety
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Margin of Safety.

hook.text: Engineers design bridges to hold ten times the expected load. They never trust their calculations perfectly.

buildup.text: A margin of safety is the gap between what you expect and what you prepare for. It is a buffer against surprise.

discovery.text: Benjamin Graham introduced this to investing. Buy a stock only when its price is well below its estimated value.

twist.text: Margin of safety works because estimates are always wrong. The question is not if your forecast errs, but by how much.

climax.text: Build buffers into every plan. Extra time, extra money, extra capacity.

punchline.text: Plans go wrong. Buffers keep you standing.

quiz.question: Who introduced the margin of safety concept to investing?
